extracted.intended_audience: small business owners, marketers, and PR professionals
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for drafting AP style (newsroom-ready) press releases that journalists can copy/paste, covering headline, dateline, lead, body structure, AP-specific grammar/format rules, and distribution conventions. Intended to make releases look professional and maximize pickup.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow AP Stylebook formatting rules
rubrics_metrics.description: An AP style press release follows the formatting rules of the Associated Press Stylebook — the gold standard for journalists and media outlets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make the release fit seamlessly into a newsroom so a journalist can copy and paste straight into their publication. This encompasses grammar, punctuation, capitalization, dateline format, neutral tone, and other AP conventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistent grammar, capitalization, and punctuation
rubrics_metrics.description: Use consistent grammar, capitalization, and punctuation throughout the release so it appears professional and newsroom-ready.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow AP capitalization rules (only proper nouns and formal titles before names are capitalized). Avoid misplaced commas and inconsistent number formats. Use consistent font (e.g., Times New Roman or Arial, 12 pt).

rubrics_metrics.name: Standardized dateline (city/state – date) formatting
rubrics_metrics.description: Format the dateline in AP style: CITY in all caps, state abbreviated per AP style, en dash before the date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: SAN FRANCISCO – August 1, 2025. If unsure how to structure the dateline, consult an AP style dateline guide for examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Neutral, factual tone
rubrics_metrics.description: Adopt a neutral, factual tone rather than promotional language so the release reads like news.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarity wins over cleverness in AP style; be factual, not promotional, especially in headlines and the lead.

rubrics_metrics.name: Headline rules (title case, length, factual)
rubrics_metrics.description: Headlines should use title case, be factual rather than promotional, and keep under 80 characters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include the main keyword or event name if relevant. Prioritize clarity so journalists immediately understand the news.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of a subhead for additional context
rubrics_metrics.description: A subhead can add context or provide a secondary hook beneath the headline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the subhead to supply a concise supporting detail (e.g., 'New York-based company raises $5M to expand into Europe').

rubrics_metrics.name: Lead/first paragraph must answer who, what, when, where, why
rubrics_metrics.description: The first paragraph (the 'lead') must deliver the facts fast by including who is making the announcement, what is happening, when and where, and why it matters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Place the dateline and then a succinct opening sentence covering who/what/when/where/why. Example lead structure included in the guide.

rubrics_metrics.name: Body structure: second paragraph, supporting details, quotes, CTA
rubrics_metrics.description: After the lead, expand logically: second paragraph for supporting details/background/stats, include quotes, and finish with a call-to-action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide specifics like partnerships, product specs, event agenda, or metrics. Use quotes to add human voice and credibility; end with a clear CTA (visit website, register, contact).

rubrics_metrics.name: Quotes and attribution format
rubrics_metrics.description: All quotes must be attributed using AP-style attribution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Format: “Quote,” said Name, Title. Include a compelling quote from a CEO or spokesperson to add credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Boilerplate (About section) requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Include a 2–3 sentence boilerplate About Us section at the bottom of the release.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep it concise, summarizing the company's mission and background in a newsroom-friendly tone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Media contact information
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide clear media contact details so journalists can follow up.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include Name, Email, and Phone (and any other relevant contact instructions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Length guideline
rubrics_metrics.description: Keep the press release concise: typically one page, two max.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim for 400–600 words — enough to give context but not so much it reads like an essay.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use 'FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE' or indicate embargo
rubrics_metrics.description: Begin with 'FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE' unless the release is embargoed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If embargoed, specify the release date/time instead of using 'FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Numbers formatting
rubrics_metrics.description: Spell out numbers one through nine; use numerals for 10 and above in AP style.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be consistent throughout the release to avoid signaling inexperience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dates formatting
rubrics_metrics.description: Write dates in AP format, e.g., 'Aug. 1, 2025' — abbreviate most months and do not use ordinal indicators ('th').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow AP conventions for month abbreviations and punctuation.

rubrics_metrics.name: State abbreviations per AP
rubrics_metrics.description: Use AP abbreviations for states (e.g., Calif.), while recognizing some states are never abbreviated (e.g., Texas, Ohio).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the AP list of state abbreviations to remain consistent with newsroom expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capitalization rules in body copy
rubrics_metrics.description: Only capitalize proper nouns and formal titles that appear before a person's name.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid over-capitalizing job descriptions or generic terms; follow AP capitalization conventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Font and presentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Use a consistent, readable font and sizing to keep the release newsroom-ready.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommended fonts: Times New Roman or Arial, 12 pt. Consistent typography reduces friction for editors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Call-to-action clarity
rubrics_metrics.description: Include a clear call-to-action telling readers what to do next (register, visit site, contact).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Place the CTA toward the end of the body in a concise sentence (e.g., 'Visit [website] to register' or 'Contact [media email] for more information').

rubrics_metrics.name: Use a template structure (FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE, dateline, lead, quote, closing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Follow a common AP-style press release template structure to ensure completeness and readability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Template elements: FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE; CITY, State – Month Day, Year; Headline (Title Case); Opening sentence with who/what/when/where/why; supporting paragraphs; quote with attribution; boilerplate; media contact.
